title: Intraocular Pressure and Anterior Segment Morphometry Changes after Uneventful Phacoemulsification in Type 2 Diabetic and Nondiabetic Patients

license.statement: CC BY, version not stated (article <license>: distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License)

indication: normal eyes: nonglaucomatous open-angle eyes with age-related cataract, preoperative IOP not above 25 mmHg, no prior eye surgery; groups by type 2 diabetes (diabetic, without severe NPDR, PDR or macular edema) versus age- and sex-matched nondiabetic patients (prospective observational, one eye per patient)

groups.description: uneventful coaxial clear-cornea phacoemulsification with in-the-bag IOL in patients with type 2 diabetes
uneventful coaxial clear-cornea phacoemulsification with in-the-bag IOL in nondiabetic patients

exclusions.what: Table 3 strata by preoperative IOP (10-14, 15-16, 17-18, 19-20, 21-25 mmHg) within each group, preoperative IOP and 6-month change
exclusions.reason: the strata partition the same eyes as the Table 2 group series (would duplicate them); they are defined by binning the series' own reference IOP and carry only the 6-month follow-up, so the study's design groups with the 1- and 6-month time course are extracted instead (extraction ambiguity: brief's subgroup rule addresses a table reporting both a cohort and its subgroups)

exclusions.what: Results text: eyes with IOP reduction/no change/increase and their means
exclusions.reason: subsets defined by the postoperative outcome
values of other studies, not this cohort

exclusions.what: Figure 1 (correlation of preoperative IOP with 6-month change)

notes: Reference kind: nonglaucomatous eyes; no glaucoma medication or washout is described, so the preoperative IOP is recorded as measured in untreated eyes.
Tonometry: Goldmann applanation tonometry, average of two readings (median of three if they differed by more than 2 mmHg), measured at the same time of day as the baseline visit (Methods 2.3).
Both groups are patient-condition subgroups (diabetes status) receiving the same standard cataract surgery, so both are control groups.
Postoperative care: topical dexamethasone, flurbiprofen and levofloxacin for 1 week then tapered over 3 weeks (both groups).
